label: AI Act Profiling & Bias Assessment
description: Bias and fundamental-rights assessment for high-risk AI systems at the intersection of the EU AI Act (high-risk Annex III, Art. 27 FRIA, data-governance, human-oversight) and GDPR (Art. 22 automated decisions, Art. 9 special-category data, DPIA). Covers the high-risk classification decision, the FRIA/DPIA interface, protected-attribute and proxy bias testing, fairness metrics, human-oversight design, and explanation rights.

claudeKnowledge.description: EU AI Act (EU) 2024/1689 (Annex III high-risk, Art. 9 risk management, Art. 10 data governance, Art. 14 human oversight, Art. 15 accuracy/robustness, Art. 27 FRIA); GDPR (EU) 2016/679 (Art. 5 fairness, Art. 9 special categories, Art. 22 automated decisions, Art. 35 DPIA); EDPB Guidelines on automated decision-making and profiling; EDPB DPIA guidance; national DPA guidance on ADM and AI

guidedInputs.label: Known Issues, Findings, or Concerns
guidedInputs.description: Describe the model, the decision it drives, any disparity already observed, prior audit/DPA findings, and what data you do or do not hold on protected attributes.
guidedInputs.placeholder: e.g. Gradient-boosted credit model declines ~18% of applicants; internal review found a 9pp approval-rate gap between two postcode clusters that correlate with ethnicity; we do not collect ethnicity, so we cannot measure disparate impact directly; reviewers rubber-stamp 96% of model recommendations; adverse-action letters give only a generic reason code...

exampleInput: We are a Swedish consumer-lender (deployer, ~300 staff) about to put a new gradient-boosted credit-decisioning model into service across the Nordics. It scores all retail applicants and auto-declines below a cutoff; ~22% of decisions are made with no human looking at the file. Legal has confirmed this is an Annex III(5)(b) creditworthiness use case and therefore high-risk, and that the auto-decline is a solely-automated decision under GDPR Art. 22. We have a 2023 DPIA but no FRIA, and we have never tested the model for disparate impact because we do not collect race or ethnicity. An internal review found a 9 percentage-point approval-rate gap between two postcode clusters that our data-science team believes correlate with ethnic origin and migration background. Reviewers who do see flagged files override the model in under 4% of cases. Adverse-action letters cite only a numeric reason code. Please (1) confirm the high-risk classification and the Art. 22 basis, (2) design a coherent FRIA-and-DPIA so we do not run two overlapping assessments, (3) give us a defensible protected-attribute and proxy bias-testing methodology — including how we can measure disparate impact without unlawfully collecting Art. 9 data — with the right fairness metrics for a credit cutoff, and (4) tell us what is broken in our human-oversight and explanation set-up.

exampleValues.known_concerns: Annex III(5)(b) high-risk credit model auto-declines ~22% of applicants with no human review. 2023 DPIA exists; no FRIA. Never tested for disparate impact because race/ethnicity not collected. 9pp approval gap between two postcode clusters believed to correlate with ethnic origin. Human reviewers override <4% of model recommendations. Adverse-action letters give only a numeric reason code.
